CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. Patient reports injury occurred on Sunday while skiing approximately 4 days ago. She was attempting moguls when her strap caught on her finger, causing it to bend backward/hyperextend. Patient has tried ice and ibuprofen without adequate relief. Pain is worse with movement.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation
Appendectomy at age 18

MEDICATIONS
Miralax

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skier

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Tenderness over distal phalanx of right index finger. Tenderness over distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Pain with flexion. Able to bend and extend finger. Able to touch thumb with affected finger. No deformity noted.

RESULTS
X-ray of right index finger: Normal, no fractures, good alignment

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion on tip of finger, no fracture. Recommend aluminum foam splint. Prescribed Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately one week. Patient to call and return if no improvement.
